input.summary: Across 1.8432–1.9564 eV the WSe2 response is dominated by two resonances that sit at one energy, about 1.870 eV. I take this to be the A2s exciton, about 130 meV above A1s. The first-order ~249 cm-1 mode peaks at 1.8703 eV (height ~80) and again at 1.8999 eV (~53), which puts the outgoing photon at ~1.869 eV. Both are consistent with an incoming and an outgoing resonance with the same state. The 480–510 cm-1 band is a second-order (two-phonon) feature. It is enhanced about 10–20× at 1.9325 eV (height ~108, FWHM ~3 cm-1, centred at 492.7 cm-1), where the scattered photon is at 1.8714 eV, the same ~1.87 eV state. At 1.9325 eV the band is far sharper than the ~7 cm-1 off-resonance profile and shifts down by ~2 cm-1. The only feature in that region that stays the same is the Si 520 cm-1 residual, which is a substrate leak and not WSe2.

observations.finding: The 480–510 cm-1 band is a narrow, strongly resonant feature when the scattered photon is at the A2s-like state, not at A1s.
observations.evidence: Height of the strongest point in 486–502 cm-1 versus excitation: 1.9564 eV: 5.6; 1.9409: 8.0; 1.9325: 108; 1.9258: 32; 1.9115: 9.4; 1.8999: 5.0; 1.8847: 0.9; 1.8703: 9.9; 1.8432: ~0.2. The peak is 13× the 1.9409 eV value and 3.4× the 1.9258 eV value. The scattered photon at 1.9325 eV (shift 492.7 cm-1 = 61.1 meV) is at 1.8714 eV. The neighbouring spectra put the scattered photon at 1.8795 eV (1.9409 eV) and 1.8647 eV (1.9258 eV), so the profile is narrow, with a half-width of roughly 5 meV or less in intensity. The 1.8703 eV (incoming) point is only ~10, so the enhancement is much stronger on the outgoing side.

observations.finding: The band is a composite whose line shape and position change with excitation, so at least two components with different resonance profiles overlap.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fits: the main peak is 494.5 cm-1 with FWHM ~7 cm-1 at 1.9564 and 1.9409 eV. It moves to 492.7 cm-1 with FWHM ~3.0 cm-1 at 1.9325 eV, and 493.0 cm-1 with FWHM ~4 cm-1 at 1.9258 eV. At 1.9325 eV a second resolved component appears at ~496.3 cm-1 (FWHM ~3.7 cm-1, height ~61, i.e. ~55% of the main peak). At 1.9115–1.8847 eV the main peak sits at 494.7–497 cm-1. At 1.8703 eV it is broad again (~6.5 cm-1) at 495.6 cm-1. A shift of 2–4 cm-1 together with narrowing is not a strain or temperature effect, because all spectra were taken on one spot at 4 K. Fit parameters are poorly constrained, so the positions carry roughly ±1 cm-1 uncertainty.

observations.finding: The first-order ~249 cm-1 mode shows incoming and outgoing resonances with the same state at ~1.870 eV, which fixes the A2s energy.
observations.evidence: Height of the ~248–250 cm-1 peak: 0.4 (1.9564 eV), 0.6 (1.9409), 2.6 (1.9325), 4.0 (1.9258), 11.6 (1.9115), 52.7 (1.8999), 6.5 (1.8847), 79.9 (1.8703), 3.4 (1.8432). At 1.8703 eV the incoming photon matches ~1.870 eV. At 1.8999 eV the scattered photon is at 1.8999 − 0.0310 = 1.869 eV. The dip at 1.8847 eV, midway between the two, is consistent with a resonance of width ≲10 meV. The ~259–263 cm-1 shoulder follows the same resonance profile (20.6 at 1.8703 eV).

observations.finding: Interpretation: the 490–500 cm-1 band is most likely second-order (an overtone or combination of ~250 cm-1 and nearby modes) and resonates through the same ~1.87 eV state. It does not behave like an A1s feature.
observations.evidence: Two times the 249 cm-1 mode is ~498 cm-1, close to the observed 493–497 cm-1. The resonance condition is also consistent: with incoming photon at 1.8703 eV and one 31 meV phonon, the first-order mode is resonant, and for the two-phonon feature the outgoing photon is at ~1.871 eV at 1.9325 eV excitation (laser − 61 meV). The mode assignment is not proven by these data, since parallel-minus-crossed polarization only restricts the symmetry. The 1s resonance is not covered by the series. A1s at 1.740 eV would need a laser at ~1.771 eV (one 31 meV phonon) or ~1.801 eV (the 61 meV feature), far below the lowest excitation of 1.8432 eV.

observations.finding: A2s sits about 130 meV above A1s, which is plausible for hBN-encapsulated monolayer WSe2.
observations.evidence: A2s ≈ 1.870 eV (±~0.004 eV, limited by the coarse excitation step) minus A1s = 1.740 eV gives ≈130 meV. This is only the 1s–2s splitting. A binding energy would need the band gap or a 3s state, which are not measured here.

observations.finding: The ~398 cm-1 line is resonant at the same state, but it is weak, and I cannot assign it.
observations.evidence: Height of ~395–401 cm-1 peak: 1.7 (1.8703 eV), 0.9 (1.9258 eV), 0.4 (1.9115 eV and 1.8432 eV), and ≤0.3 elsewhere. Peaks near the noise floor (~0.1–0.2) are tentative.

observations.finding: The Si 520 cm-1 peak is an artifact of the substrate and not WSe2; it overlaps the high-shift end of the 490–510 band.
observations.evidence: Height ~2.5–3.5 in all nine spectra (position 519.4–520.3 cm-1, FWHM ~3.5–4 cm-1), including the on-resonance 1.9325 eV spectrum where WSe2 features jump by >10×. caveats: Excitation step is a few meV. The 490–500 cm-1 resonance is narrower than that (~5 meV or less), so the resonance maximum, width and peak height are undersampled. The true peak could lie between 1.9258 and 1.9409 eV, and the ~108 height at 1.9325 eV is a lower bound on the true on-resonance value. The 2s energy is only good to about ±4 meV.

The resonance energy is deduced from a single energy axis (laser energy minus phonon energy). With only 9 points I cannot separate incoming from outgoing enhancement unambiguously for the 490 band. Fitting a proper Raman-excitation-profile model (Lorentzian incoming and outgoing terms, with a damping term) would need a denser scan.

Parallel minus crossed polarization subtracts two independent measurements. This produces dispersive or negative artifacts near strong peaks (minimum −2.1 at ~229 cm-1 for 1.8999 eV; −1.2 near 300 cm-1 for 1.9115 eV; −1.1 near 479 cm-1 and negative lobes on both sides of the 1.9325 eV peak). A small polarization-dependent spectrometer response or a slight energy shift between channels can also distort peak positions and widths by 1–2 cm-1.

The sub-structure at 1.9325 eV (492.7 plus ~496.3 cm-1) rests on two Lorentzians. The 3.6 cm-1 spacing is comparable to the resolution and to the lobe artifacts. Treat it as plausible, not proven. The Si 520 cm-1 tail and baseline were also fitted simultaneously and add correlated error.

Absolute scattering probabilities depend on the interference correction for 290 nm SiO2 / hBN layers and on normalizing to Si 520 cm-1 at each wavelength. Any wavelength-dependent error (hBN thickness, laser focus, absorption in the Si) feeds directly into the apparent resonance profile, though a 10–20× enhancement is well beyond such effects.

Possible alternative: the 490 band could include a hBN or substrate-related feature or overlap with Si second-order scattering below 520 cm-1. The strong, narrow and resonant behavior argues against this, but the broad off-resonance component (FWHM ~7 cm-1 at 1.9564, 1.9409 and 1.8703 eV) is consistent with an unresolved sum of modes.

The identification of ~1.87 eV as A2s is made from the 1s–2s spacing and typical values, not from a direct measurement on this sample (no PL, reflectance or photoluminescence-excitation spectrum). Other excited states, a charged-exciton replica or a nearby B-exciton-related feature (B is expected ~0.4 eV higher) are alternatives I consider unlikely but cannot exclude.

The dye laser steps through a very wide range, so laser power and spot position may vary slightly between steps. Under 100 µW at 4 K the exciton may still heat or photodope locally; the data cannot show whether doping changed between steps.
questions_for_user: Do you have a PL or reflectance/PLE spectrum from the same spot? It would fix the A2s energy and linewidth directly and replace my inference of ~1.870 eV from the Raman resonances.

Can you add excitation steps of ~1–2 meV between 1.920 and 1.945 eV (and 1.865–1.905 eV for the first-order mode)? This would resolve the width of the narrow resonance and separate incoming from outgoing enhancement.

Was the parallel and crossed data taken on the same spot with the same grating position and acquisition time, and was the spectrometer polarization response calibrated? This sets how much of the negative lobes and the 1–2 cm-1 position shifts is instrumental.

What are the sample-spot position, laser power at each step and the spot size? A drift in focus or power of tens of percent would not explain the 10–20× enhancement, but it matters for the absolute values.

Can you provide the Raman spectrum at a nonresonant energy in unpolarized or co-polarized configuration, plus the hBN thicknesses? That would allow verifying the interference correction and the assignment of the 490–500 cm-1 band to second-order modes.
citations: Stier, A. V. et al., Nano Lett. 16, 7054 (2016), probing the influence of dielectric environment on excitons in monolayer WSe2 (recalled from memory for the 1s–2s splitting; not re-verified, no specific figure or table named).
No other literature was consulted; assignments of the ~249 and ~398 cm-1 modes and of the 490–500 cm-1 band are my inference from the resonance profiles and are not checked against a specific paper.
limits: These spectra cannot tell the phonon assignment of the 490–500 cm-1 band (overtone versus combination), the exciton–phonon coupling strength, or whether the resonance is through a 2s exciton or another state close to 1.87 eV.
They contain no information on A1s resonance (the lowest excitation is 1.8432 eV, ~100 meV above A1s), so nothing here constrains the 1s Raman response, the exciton linewidths, or the binding energy.
The data cannot separate defects, doping or strain; no D-type or intensity-ratio reference was measured, and the on-resonance narrowing says nothing about sample homogeneity beyond this one spot.
Resonance widths and energies are limited by the few-meV excitation step and by the number of points (nine), so no quantitative excitation-profile fit is justified.

structured_output.summary: Across 1.8432–1.9564 eV the WSe2 response is dominated by two resonances that sit at one energy, about 1.870 eV. I take this to be the A2s exciton, about 130 meV above A1s. The first-order ~249 cm-1 mode peaks at 1.8703 eV (height ~80) and again at 1.8999 eV (~53), which puts the outgoing photon at ~1.869 eV. Both are consistent with an incoming and an outgoing resonance with the same state. The 480–510 cm-1 band is a second-order (two-phonon) feature. It is enhanced about 10–20× at 1.9325 eV (height ~108, FWHM ~3 cm-1, centred at 492.7 cm-1), where the scattered photon is at 1.8714 eV, the same ~1.87 eV state. At 1.9325 eV the band is far sharper than the ~7 cm-1 off-resonance profile and shifts down by ~2 cm-1. The only feature in that region that stays the same is the Si 520 cm-1 residual, which is a substrate leak and not WSe2.

observations.finding: The 480–510 cm-1 band is a narrow, strongly resonant feature when the scattered photon is at the A2s-like state, not at A1s.
observations.evidence: Height of the strongest point in 486–502 cm-1 versus excitation: 1.9564 eV: 5.6; 1.9409: 8.0; 1.9325: 108; 1.9258: 32; 1.9115: 9.4; 1.8999: 5.0; 1.8847: 0.9; 1.8703: 9.9; 1.8432: ~0.2. The peak is 13× the 1.9409 eV value and 3.4× the 1.9258 eV value. The scattered photon at 1.9325 eV (shift 492.7 cm-1 = 61.1 meV) is at 1.8714 eV. The neighbouring spectra put the scattered photon at 1.8795 eV (1.9409 eV) and 1.8647 eV (1.9258 eV), so the profile is narrow, with a half-width of roughly 5 meV or less in intensity. The 1.8703 eV (incoming) point is only ~10, so the enhancement is much stronger on the outgoing side.

observations.finding: The band is a composite whose line shape and position change with excitation, so at least two components with different resonance profiles overlap.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fits: the main peak is 494.5 cm-1 with FWHM ~7 cm-1 at 1.9564 and 1.9409 eV. It moves to 492.7 cm-1 with FWHM ~3.0 cm-1 at 1.9325 eV, and 493.0 cm-1 with FWHM ~4 cm-1 at 1.9258 eV. At 1.9325 eV a second resolved component appears at ~496.3 cm-1 (FWHM ~3.7 cm-1, height ~61, i.e. ~55% of the main peak). At 1.9115–1.8847 eV the main peak sits at 494.7–497 cm-1. At 1.8703 eV it is broad again (~6.5 cm-1) at 495.6 cm-1. A shift of 2–4 cm-1 together with narrowing is not a strain or temperature effect, because all spectra were taken on one spot at 4 K. Fit parameters are poorly constrained, so the positions carry roughly ±1 cm-1 uncertainty.

observations.finding: The first-order ~249 cm-1 mode shows incoming and outgoing resonances with the same state at ~1.870 eV, which fixes the A2s energy.
observations.evidence: Height of the ~248–250 cm-1 peak: 0.4 (1.9564 eV), 0.6 (1.9409), 2.6 (1.9325), 4.0 (1.9258), 11.6 (1.9115), 52.7 (1.8999), 6.5 (1.8847), 79.9 (1.8703), 3.4 (1.8432). At 1.8703 eV the incoming photon matches ~1.870 eV. At 1.8999 eV the scattered photon is at 1.8999 − 0.0310 = 1.869 eV. The dip at 1.8847 eV, midway between the two, is consistent with a resonance of width ≲10 meV. The ~259–263 cm-1 shoulder follows the same resonance profile (20.6 at 1.8703 eV).

observations.finding: Interpretation: the 490–500 cm-1 band is most likely second-order (an overtone or combination of ~250 cm-1 and nearby modes) and resonates through the same ~1.87 eV state. It does not behave like an A1s feature.
observations.evidence: Two times the 249 cm-1 mode is ~498 cm-1, close to the observed 493–497 cm-1. The resonance condition is also consistent: with incoming photon at 1.8703 eV and one 31 meV phonon, the first-order mode is resonant, and for the two-phonon feature the outgoing photon is at ~1.871 eV at 1.9325 eV excitation (laser − 61 meV). The mode assignment is not proven by these data, since parallel-minus-crossed polarization only restricts the symmetry. The 1s resonance is not covered by the series. A1s at 1.740 eV would need a laser at ~1.771 eV (one 31 meV phonon) or ~1.801 eV (the 61 meV feature), far below the lowest excitation of 1.8432 eV.

observations.finding: A2s sits about 130 meV above A1s, which is plausible for hBN-encapsulated monolayer WSe2.
observations.evidence: A2s ≈ 1.870 eV (±~0.004 eV, limited by the coarse excitation step) minus A1s = 1.740 eV gives ≈130 meV. This is only the 1s–2s splitting. A binding energy would need the band gap or a 3s state, which are not measured here.
observations.source: Typical hBN-encapsulated WSe2 1s–2s splitting of about 130–135 meV, recalled from Stier et al., Nano Lett. 2016 (WSe2 dielectric screening). I did not check the paper, so the exact value and table or figure are unverified.

observations.finding: The ~398 cm-1 line is resonant at the same state, but it is weak, and I cannot assign it.
observations.evidence: Height of ~395–401 cm-1 peak: 1.7 (1.8703 eV), 0.9 (1.9258 eV), 0.4 (1.9115 eV and 1.8432 eV), and ≤0.3 elsewhere. Peaks near the noise floor (~0.1–0.2) are tentative.

observations.finding: The Si 520 cm-1 peak is an artifact of the substrate and not WSe2; it overlaps the high-shift end of the 490–510 band.
observations.evidence: Height ~2.5–3.5 in all nine spectra (position 519.4–520.3 cm-1, FWHM ~3.5–4 cm-1), including the on-resonance 1.9325 eV spectrum where WSe2 features jump by >10×. Because Si 520 cm-1 is also the intensity calibration reference, its constancy is partly by construction and is not independent evidence of calibration quality. It leaks through the parallel-minus-crossed subtraction, and at 1.9325 eV its fit height (2.5) is distorted by the neighbouring negative lobes.

caveats: Excitation step is a few meV. The 490–500 cm-1 resonance is narrower than that (~5 meV or less), so the resonance maximum, width and peak height are undersampled. The true peak could lie between 1.9258 and 1.9409 eV, and the ~108 height at 1.9325 eV is a lower bound on the true on-resonance value. The 2s energy is only good to about ±4 meV.

The resonance energy is deduced from a single energy axis (laser energy minus phonon energy). With only 9 points I cannot separate incoming from outgoing enhancement unambiguously for the 490 band. Fitting a proper Raman-excitation-profile model (Lorentzian incoming and outgoing terms, with a damping term) would need a denser scan.

Parallel minus crossed polarization subtracts two independent measurements. This produces dispersive or negative artifacts near strong peaks (minimum −2.1 at ~229 cm-1 for 1.8999 eV; −1.2 near 300 cm-1 for 1.9115 eV; −1.1 near 479 cm-1 and negative lobes on both sides of the 1.9325 eV peak). A small polarization-dependent spectrometer response or a slight energy shift between channels can also distort peak positions and widths by 1–2 cm-1.

The sub-structure at 1.9325 eV (492.7 plus ~496.3 cm-1) rests on two Lorentzians. The 3.6 cm-1 spacing is comparable to the resolution and to the lobe artifacts. Treat it as plausible, not proven. The Si 520 cm-1 tail and baseline were also fitted simultaneously and add correlated error.

Absolute scattering probabilities depend on the interference correction for 290 nm SiO2 / hBN layers and on normalizing to Si 520 cm-1 at each wavelength. Any wavelength-dependent error (hBN thickness, laser focus, absorption in the Si) feeds directly into the apparent resonance profile, though a 10–20× enhancement is well beyond such effects.

Possible alternative: the 490 band could include a hBN or substrate-related feature or overlap with Si second-order scattering below 520 cm-1. The strong, narrow and resonant behavior argues against this, but the broad off-resonance component (FWHM ~7 cm-1 at 1.9564, 1.9409 and 1.8703 eV) is consistent with an unresolved sum of modes.

The identification of ~1.87 eV as A2s is made from the 1s–2s spacing and typical values, not from a direct measurement on this sample (no PL, reflectance or photoluminescence-excitation spectrum). Other excited states, a charged-exciton replica or a nearby B-exciton-related feature (B is expected ~0.4 eV higher) are alternatives I consider unlikely but cannot exclude.

The dye laser steps through a very wide range, so laser power and spot position may vary slightly between steps. Under 100 µW at 4 K the exciton may still heat or photodope locally; the data cannot show whether doping changed between steps.
questions_for_user: Do you have a PL or reflectance/PLE spectrum from the same spot? It would fix the A2s energy and linewidth directly and replace my inference of ~1.870 eV from the Raman resonances.

Can you add excitation steps of ~1–2 meV between 1.920 and 1.945 eV (and 1.865–1.905 eV for the first-order mode)? This would resolve the width of the narrow resonance and separate incoming from outgoing enhancement.

Was the parallel and crossed data taken on the same spot with the same grating position and acquisition time, and was the spectrometer polarization response calibrated? This sets how much of the negative lobes and the 1–2 cm-1 position shifts is instrumental.

What are the sample-spot position, laser power at each step and the spot size? A drift in focus or power of tens of percent would not explain the 10–20× enhancement, but it matters for the absolute values.

Can you provide the Raman spectrum at a nonresonant energy in unpolarized or co-polarized configuration, plus the hBN thicknesses? That would allow verifying the interference correction and the assignment of the 490–500 cm-1 band to second-order modes.

limits: These spectra cannot tell the phonon assignment of the 490–500 cm-1 band (overtone versus combination), the exciton–phonon coupling strength, or whether the resonance is through a 2s exciton or another state close to 1.87 eV.
They contain no information on A1s resonance (the lowest excitation is 1.8432 eV, ~100 meV above A1s), so nothing here constrains the 1s Raman response, the exciton linewidths, or the binding energy.
The data cannot separate defects, doping or strain; no D-type or intensity-ratio reference was measured, and the on-resonance narrowing says nothing about sample homogeneity beyond this one spot.
Resonance widths and energies are limited by the few-meV excitation step and by the number of points (nine), so no quantitative excitation-profile fit is justified.
